question.prompt: Three cubes of volume \(1,\) \(8\) and \(27\) are glued together at their faces. The smallest possible surface area of the resulting configuration is

solutions.explanation:
Gluing hides surface area, so minimizing the exposed area means maximizing the area of contact. A cube of edge length \(s\) has volume \(s^3\), so the three edge lengths are \(1\), \(2\), and \(3\). Before gluing, their surface areas total
\[
6(1^2+2^2+3^2)=6(14)=84.
\]
Each contact patch hides its area twice, once on each cube. For each pair, the contact area cannot exceed one face of the smaller cube. Thus the contacts between the \(2\)- and \(3\)-cubes, the \(1\)- and \(3\)-cubes, and the \(1\)- and \(2\)-cubes have areas at most \(4\), \(1\), and \(1\), respectively. Every configuration therefore has exposed area at least
\[
84-2(4+1+1)=72.
\]
To attain this bound, place the two smaller cubes side by side on one \(3\times3\) face of the largest cube, with their front edges aligned and their adjacent sides touching. Their footprints fit because their combined width is \(2+1=3\) and their greatest depth is \(2\). Their bases give contact areas \(4\) and \(1\), and they share a full \(1\times1\) side face, giving the third contact area \(1\).

Thus the lower bound is attainable, and the smallest surface area is \(\boxed{72}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
solutions.title: Maximize the hidden face area
